_doc: OCTOPUS fleet metadata - machine-readable handoff. Generated 2026-09-15 by the hardware-enrollment lane. Every field below was MEASURED on the live boards, not inferred. See EVIDENCE.md for the raw command output.

red_boundaries: no secret/token/.env/seed/wallet value may be printed, sent, copied or committed - key NAMES only
no receipt-chain entry may be deleted or rewritten
no PASS or LIVE may be declared without a same-scope receipt
never power off board 138 (it is the executor; the organism dies with it)
governance.may_authorize: false on EVERY node - do not raise it without an owner decision

network.note_on_router_api: Every /goform/* endpoint (including stokCfg) returns 302 to /login.html. GOAHEAD_AES_CRYPT=y means the AES login needs a server sign that is itself behind that redirect. Do NOT brute-force: only 5 attempts remain before lockout. Use a TCP scan of the /24 instead; it is sufficient and was used for every census here.

access.method: ssh key auth only - no passwords anywhere
key_names_only: C:/Users/Armin/.ssh/octopus_mesh_ed25519  (on 138; reaches ALL 7 nodes - the mesh identity)
access.trap: When scripting from 138, run as the user that owns the key. The registry 'identity' field is the key path ON THAT NODE (/root/.ssh/... for non-138 nodes) and is NOT readable by user 'ari'. From 138 always use ~/.ssh/octopus_mesh_ed25519 to reach every peer.

mesh_registry.trap_1: octomesh_agent_bridge transmit() raises KeyError if a node entry is REMOVED. Mark retired:true instead of deleting.
mesh_registry.trap_2: node 138's entry is self-referential; its mesh key was added to its own authorized_keys so it verifies like the others (7/7).

traps_learned_the_hard_way.mac_follows_boot_medium: 193 and 114 each presented a DIFFERENT MAC after booting from eMMC vs SD. Do not treat the MAC as a stable board identity.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.hostnamectl_fails_over_ssh: dbus is broken over SSH on these boards -> hostnamectl errors. Write /etc/hostname directly and use `hostname <name>`.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.no_sftp_server: DietPi/Dropbear boards reject scp (`/usr/lib/sftp-server: No such file or directory`). Stream instead: ssh host 'cat > /path' < localfile
traps_learned_the_hard_way.xz_often_missing: The DietPi images had no xz and no python3; install xz-utils or use python3's lzma. A previous flash silently wrote 0 bytes because xz was absent.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.hot_plug_is_NOT_the_evil: The 'never hot-plug SD' rule overstated things. 138 and the Plus both hot-plugged cards cleanly. The 182 crashes were caused by a FAULTY CARD wedging the SD controller, not by hot-plug itself. Still: power off when you can, and never on 138.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.sd_boot_hides_the_emmc: When the Plus booted from SD, Linux never brought its eMMC up (controller init, clocks running, no card found). Boot from eMMC instead and it works perfectly. Do not conclude 'hardware fault' from 'software identical' without varying the BOOT MEDIUM - that mistake was made here and later falsified.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.bash_heredoc_over_ssh: Single quotes inside an `ssh host '...'` string terminate it. Use double quotes outside with <<'EOF' inside, or pipe the script via `ssh host 'cat > /tmp/x.sh' < file`.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.ssh_consumes_stdin: A python script that shells out to ssh must pass stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL or ssh eats the script's own heredoc.
traps_learned_the_hard_way.crlf: Strip CR from authorized_keys and any script (sed -i 's/\r$//') or keys/scripts silently fail.
